scene: Inferno XV — Brunetto Latini and the moving conversation on the raised bank
story: Dante and Virgil continue on the raised stone bank beside the stream through the burning sand, where the banks shield them from falling fire.
A band of spirits under the fiery rain approaches; Brunetto Latini recognizes Dante and takes hold of his garment.
Dante recognizes his former teacher, respectfully lowers his head and speaks with him while walking along the embankment.
Brunetto explains that he must not halt: stopping would subject him to a different punishment, so he continues moving below while Dante walks above.
Brunetto foretells that Dante will suffer hostility and exile; Dante acknowledges the guidance he received from his teacher.
Dante asks about others among the band and promises to preserve Brunetto's account.
Brunetto departs running to rejoin the moving souls, compared by Dante to a victorious runner at Verona; Dante and Virgil continue their journey.
